newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel rises on trader's purchase.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel rises on trader's purchase.

text.p: The Singapore gas oil market continued its upswing due to a buying spree from a Singapore oil trader who bought a total of 500,000 barrels on Thursday, traders said.
The purchases on Thursday were for end March and early April cargoes at $26.10 per barrel from a European major, at $26.80 from another major and at $26.60 from a Western trader.
The same trader bought 220,000 barrels on Wednesday at $25.95.

Traders said the deal levels were much too high, indicating a 30-50 cents premium to the swaps values for March. This was despite the swaps price itself being pulled up by the strong high levels traded on the physical market.
They said the trader had bought a total of two million barrels of gas oil swaps on Wednesday and overnight which spurred prices upwards.

Some traders noted that the current high gas oil values would not be sustained once the trader withdraws from the market as regional demand remained thin. The spectre of large volumes of arbitrage cargoes due to arrive in Asia during end March or early April also continued to spook the market.
A U.S. major was seen buying about 30,000 tonnes of gas oil at a premium of $1.00 per barrel to Singapore spot quotes for early April delivery to Hong Kong, on a c-and-f basis.
Taiwan has also issued a tender to sell 0.3-percent sulphur diesel for end-April lifting fob, which closes on March 12.
After buying around 4.0 million barrels of gas oil for March, Indonesia was expected to buy over 3.0 million barrels for April.
Indonesia's jet fuel requirements for April were projected at around 1.5 million barrels, about the same volume as in March.
India was expected to take only one kerosene cargo in its tender for April arrival. The tender closed on March 6 and was expected to be awarded by late Friday.
The swaps March jet/gas oil regrade firmed to $2.00/$2.40 per barrel up from Wednesday's bid of $1.90.
